answer: One copper prospector works a dune claim with a 150 token deposit frozen 120 days and a 95 dollar license. An opal stone marks the corner, and the surveyor issues copper sample tags. Each week the prospector pans a kilo of dune sand, weighs the grains and logs the yield with the tag in the photo. A neighbor signs the tally, and the surveyor checks twice. A forged yield forfeits the deposit and bars the applicant 180 days. Faking 10,000 claims freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 950,000 dollars. A fake claim leaves footprints across the dune, and they lead the surveyor to an empty pocket.
